chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has a slave girl and intends to emancipate her and then marry her: does he make her emancipation her dowry, or does he emancipate her then give her a dowry? And is there a waiting period for her from him, and how long is her waiting period if he emancipates her? And is it permissible for him to marry her without a dowry, and how long is her waiting period from someone else? He said: He makes her emancipation her dowry if he wishes, and if he wishes he can emancipate her then give her a dowry. And if her emancipation is her dowry, then she observes a waiting period, and it is not permissible to marry her when he emancipates her except with a dowry. And the man cannot have intercourse with the woman when he marries her until he gives her something, even if it is a dirham.
ai.seo_question: Can a man's emancipation of his slave girl serve as her dowry in marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the flexibility in marital contracts for a master marrying his freed slave girl, allowing emancipation itself to serve as the dowry (mahr) or a separate payment to be made. It emphasizes the necessity of the waiting period (iddah) and the minimum requirement of a dowry for consummation, reflecting the juristic principle that marriage is not valid without some form of consideration. This ruling highlights the transition of status from slavery to free wife within the early Shia legal framework.
